prompt: Create an edge-to-edge square native LCD settings-screen concept for Felucca, a musical instrument with a 240 by 240 logical pixel display. Render the screen alone with crisp readable text, no device, desk, browser, caption or perspective. The two reference images supply the existing M8Stealth bitmap lettering, AMBER palette, dark surfaces and utilitarian control language; they do not prescribe this new composition. Lead with a direct settings list: seven equally tall, single-line rows, stable label and right-aligned value columns. Content, in order: COLOR — AMBER; STYLE — FLAT; ANIM — ON; LEDS — DIM HI; AUTO OFF — SCREEN 15m with a small submenu chevron; SCOPE — OUT; HOME — TRACKS. LEDS is the selected row, using a solid high-contrast selection band, and its value has the same type size as every other value. No oversized focus value and no card expansion. A compact MENU header includes HOME CLOSE; the existing category strip identifies DISPLAY and provides compact CONTROL, AUDIO, MIDI, SYSTEM neighbors. A quiet 4/7 position indicator and bottom physical-control hints ALGO TAB, PRESETS ROW, K1 VALUE finish the screen. This is an overview for finding, comparing and immediately changing settings. Keep every label readable and the native pixel character convincing.
